transcript.text: Alright, let's get this coordination meeting started. We've got tomorrow's inbound delivery — one palletized lot of generator housings and one lot of communications cable reels — and I need to publish final lane assignments before the receiving crew leaves today. The draft plan currently treats all three staging lanes as interchangeable with no special receiving controls listed. Before I assign lanes, I need to hear from each of you: are there any changes or issues affecting tomorrow's receiving plan that I need to know about? Warehouse ops, movement control — what are you seeing?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Sir, there's a critical issue you need to know before assigning lanes. I confirmed this morning that only Lane 2 has a current floor-load certification for the 1,800-kilogram generator-housing pallet. That certification is filed in the warehouse binder, but it has not been added to the yard diagram yet — which is why the draft plan still shows all three lanes as interchangeable. The generator-housing pallet must go to Lane 2; the other lanes are not certified for that weight.

transcript.text: Sir, I need to report a change affecting tomorrow's receiving plan. I received the carrier's vehicle diagram this afternoon and confirmed that the cable-reel tilt-bed requires a 4.0-meter turning clearance that is only available at Lane 3. This diagram has not yet been included in the movement-control brief, which is why the draft plan doesn't reflect it. The cable reels must be staged at Lane 3 to accommodate the vehicle's turning requirements.
